עַד דָּן means “as far as Dan” and identifies the place Abram reached in pursuit.

review.translation: [And when|0] [Abram|1] [heard|0] [that|2] [his relative|4] [had been taken captive|3], [he mustered|5] [his|7] [318|10,11,12,13] [trained men|6,7] [who had been born in|8] [his household|9], [and he pursued|14] {his enemies} [as far as|15] [Dan|16].

analysis.evidence: The כִּי clause gives the content of the news Abram heard: נִשְׁבָּה אָחִיו, ‘his kinsman had been captured.’
analysis.morphology: The prefixed conjunction וַ introduces a Qal wayyiqtol, third person masculine singular, with אַבְרָם as its subject.
analysis.sense: hear news, learn of an event

draft.change: Link the existing Abram article to אבה through its father element and add Genesis 12:4 as an example.
draft.definition: Abram, son of Terah, later named Abraham. The name means “exalted father.”
draft.evidence: Genesis 12:4 repeats the name אַבְרָם when giving Abram’s age at departure. The name’s אָב element belongs to Haqor’s אבה article.

analysis.evidence: In וַיִּשְׁמַע אַבְרָם כִּי נִשְׁבָּה אָחִיו, אַבְרָם names the man who heard that his kinsman had been captured.
analysis.morphology: Hebrew personal name with no prefix or suffix.
analysis.sense: Abram, the son of Terah later named Abraham

analysis.evidence: After וַיִּשְׁמַע אַבְרָם (“Abram heard”), כִּי introduces the report Abram heard: נִשְׁבָּה אָחִיו (“his kinsman had been captured”).
analysis.morphology: Uninflected Hebrew conjunction without a prefix or suffix.
analysis.sense: that (what is seen, known or said)

analysis.evidence: כִּי נִשְׁבָּה אָחִיו gives the news Abram heard. His kinsman had been taken captive, and Abram set out in pursuit.
analysis.morphology: Niphal perfect, third person masculine singular, agreeing with the following subject אָחִיו (“his kinsman”). The initial נִ is part of the Niphal stem.

analysis.evidence: Abram hears that אָחִיו has been taken captive. Genesis 14:12 identifies the captive as Lot, the son of Abram’s brother, so אָחִיו here refers to Abram’s nephew.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular construct noun with a third-person masculine singular possessive suffix referring to Abram.

analysis.evidence: The direct object אֶת חֲנִיכָיו identifies those Abram mustered as his trained men. The verse counts 318 men born in his household and then says he pursued the captors as far as Dan.
analysis.morphology: The prefixed conjunction וַ introduces a Hiphil wayyiqtol, third-person masculine singular, with Abram as its subject.

analysis.evidence: In וַיָּרֶק אֶת חֲנִיכָיו, אֶת marks חֲנִיכָיו (“his trained men”) as the direct object of וַיָּרֶק. The possessive suffix makes the object definite.
analysis.morphology: Hebrew direct-object particle with no prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: אֶת marks חֲנִיכָיו as the object of וַיָּרֶק. The phrase יְלִידֵי בֵיתוֹ identifies the men Abram mustered as members born in his household, and the count gives their number as 318.
analysis.morphology: The adjective is used as a noun in the masculine plural construct with a third-person masculine singular possessive suffix referring to Abram.

analysis.evidence: יְלִידֵי בֵיתוֹ means “those born in his household.” The phrase identifies Abram’s trained men (חֲנִיכָיו) by their household of birth.
analysis.morphology: Masculine plural construct of יָלִיד, used substantivally. The ending ־ֵי marks the plural construct before בֵיתוֹ.

draft.change: Add Genesis 14:14 as evidence for the existing household sense of בַּיִת in article byt.
draft.definition: A person’s household, including dependents born into it.
draft.evidence: Genesis 14:14 calls Abram’s trained men יְלִידֵי בֵיתוֹ, those born in his household. Genesis 17:27 likewise counts home-born men among the men of Abraham’s household.

analysis.evidence: יְלִידֵי בֵיתוֹ, “those born in his household,” identifies the 318 trained men Abram musters. Their birth into his household explains their relationship to him.
analysis.morphology: בֵית is the masculine singular construct form of the common noun בַּיִת. The third-person masculine singular possessive suffix וֹ refers to Abram.

analysis.evidence: שְׁמֹנָה עָשָׂר means ‘eighteen’. The following וּשְׁלֹשׁ מֵאוֹת adds three hundred, bringing the count of Abram’s trained men to 318.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular absolute cardinal numeral in the form used with עָשָׂר to count males.
analysis.sense: eight as the units component of eighteen

analysis.evidence: The preceding שְׁמֹנָה supplies “eight,” and עָשָׂר supplies “-teen.” Together they form “eighteen” in the count of Abram’s 318 trained men.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular absolute cardinal numeral, without prefix or suffix.
analysis.sense: ten, in the numbers eleven to nineteen

analysis.evidence: שְׁמֹנָה עָשָׂר gives eighteen, and וּשְׁלֹשׁ מֵאוֹת adds three hundred, bringing the count of Abram’s trained men to 318.
analysis.morphology: וּ is the conjunction “and.” שְׁלֹשׁ is the feminine singular construct form of the cardinal numeral “three.” It counts מֵאוֹת, “hundreds,” so וּשְׁלֹשׁ מֵאוֹת means “and three hundred.”
Cardinal numeral, feminine plural absolute, with no prefix or suffix.
analysis.sense: hundreds (plural מֵאוֹת, with the digits: three hundred to nine hundred)

analysis.evidence: After hearing of his kinsman’s capture, Abram musters his men and pursues the captors. עַד דָּן gives the extent of the pursuit, “as far as Dan.”
analysis.morphology: The prefixed conjunction וַ and the Qal third-person masculine singular verb form a wayyiqtol. Abram is the subject.

analysis.evidence: In וַיִּרְדֹּף עַד דָּן, “he pursued as far as Dan,” עַד marks Dan as the endpoint of Abram’s pursuit.
analysis.morphology: Hebrew preposition without a prefix or suffix.
analysis.sense: as far as, up to, to (a place or person)

analysis.evidence: וַיִּרְדֹּף עַד דָּן means “he pursued as far as Dan.” The preposition עַד marks Dan as the geographical endpoint. The supplied gloss “Ramses” has no support in the text.
analysis.morphology: Hebrew proper noun used as a place name, with no prefix or suffix.
analysis.sense: Dan, the place marking the limit of Abram’s pursuit in this verse.
